transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (AE, Redwood); Rita Nair (SE, Redwood); Samir Patel (CSM, Redwood); Jules Ramirez (Head of Platform, Cobalt Orbit); Priya Shah (ML Eng); Marco Leone (Infra Eng)
Recording: Zoom

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Goal: scope POC for capacity/autoscale and fallbacks for Cobalt Orbit's conversational summarization pipeline.
- Outcomes: agree to sizing worksheet, share traces, run 2-day benchmark on reserved baseline + burst pool, validate fallback to quantized model and queueing strategy.

Topics: success criteria, baseline sizing, burst strategy, queueing/backpressure, fallback policy, security requirements, timelines

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick intros — i'm avery, i'll be owning the POC side and the commercial touchpoint. rita will drive the benchmark and infra questions. samir is on the CSM side for rollout. you guys wanna say hi?
[00:12] Jules: yeah hi i'm jules, head of platform at cobalt orbit. priya and marco here too. thanks for doing this.
[00:17] Priya: hi, i'm priya, ml eng. main ask: we need predictable tail latency under load but also keep cost in check.
[00:24] Marco: infra lead, focused on networking and peering.
[00:28] Rita: cool. just to set expectations, we'll scope a POC that proves three things: 1) we can meet p95 latency SLOs for your typical traffic, 2) autoscale from reserved baseline to burst without dropped requests, and 3) fallback behavior is acceptable to UX/product.
[00:42] Jules: sounds right. for context, our service does multi-turn summarization of customer chats. bursty traffic — mornings and product launches cause big spikes. our current in-house infra struggles with both cost and ramp.
[00:55] Priya: to add numbers: steady-state is about 40 reqs/s with an average of ~1.2k tokens per request; peak bursts hit 220 reqs/s for 2-8 minute windows. latency target is p95 < 450 ms for responses under 2k tokens.
[01:12] Avery: perfect, that's exactly the dataset we need for sizing. quick question on concurrency: is that concurrent users or queued requests?
[01:19] Priya: concurrent active requests. users also do streaming in some cases. so tail matters.
[01:24] Rita: okay. perceptual baseline: for a model like LLaMA-2-70b-8bit (quantized) or a 13b mix we typically see X tokens/sec baseline on A100 80GB; we'll propose two baselines: reserved baseline for predictable throughput and a burst pool for transient spikes.
[01:41] Marco: when you say burst pool, is that autoscaling reserved capacity or ephemeral cloud GPUs? what's the cost model?
[01:47] Avery: good question — for POC we recommend reserved GPUs for baseline (e.g., 2 x A100-80GB) to keep steady cost predictable, plus a burst pool of pre-warmed instances (hot pool) that can be scheduled when needed. the burst capacity can be either billed as on-demand or temporary reserved capacity depending on your procurement.
[02:04] Jules: procurement will prefer reserved for month-to-month but we can do mixed. can you outline fallback behaviors if burst is exhausted? we don't want 5xxs during a product launch.
[02:12] Rita: options, in order of preference: 1) queueing with backpressure and progressive responses (you show typing indicator), 2) automatically fall back to a smaller quantized model variant for some requests, 3) degrade non-critical features (e.g., remove heavy reranking), 4) rate-limit new sessions.
[02:29] Priya: i like the idea of fallback to smaller model, but we need to measure quality delta. acceptable drop in rouge/summary coherence is max 6% for our product.
[02:37] Avery: noted — so success criteria will include quality retention thresholds (e.g., <=6% drop on your eval prompts), latency SLOs, and cost per 1k requests under steady-state.
[02:47] Marco: also need audit logs for every request and key rotation via our KMS. SOC2 is required for vendor. is that covered?
[02:55] Samir: yes we will share SOC2 cert, network diagram, and the integration doc for SSO (SAML/OIDC) and KMS. that's part of the docs pack we'll send.
[03:04] Jules: great. on benchmarks, what's the plan and timing?
[03:08] Rita: proposed plan: you provide an anonymized 7-day traffic trace and a small eval set (50-100 prompts representing edge cases). we run a 2-day benchmark: day one baseline reserved config, day two baseline + burst pool with simulated spikes (replay windows). metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, effective cost per 1k requests, cache hit rates.
[03:29] Priya: will the benchmark include streaming builds? we need to validate streaming latency too.
[03:33] Rita: yes, we'll include streaming flows and KV cache warmup scenarios. note: transcriptions sometimes say "K V cash" — but we mean KV cache like key value cache for autoregressive speed-ups.
[03:43] Marco: for networking, we need a maintenance window for VPC peering and allowlist rules. how long does Redwood need to run the benchmark?
[03:50] Avery: two full days; but we can do staggered runs across your off-peak windows. we'll need firewall egress to our test runners and S3 access for trace upload or use a presigned URL — whichever you prefer.
[04:03] Jules: presigned URL is preferred. procurement asks for a pricing estimate up front — can you give ballpark for reserved+burst?
[04:10] Avery: rough sketch: baseline 2 x A100-80GB reserved -> estimated cost $X/day (we'll send real numbers in the worksheet). burst pool: pre-warmed hot pool of 4 instances that can be spun to handle peak; cost depends on how long they're kept hot. we'll supply a cost model that shows tradeoffs: lower latency vs. reserved commit.
[04:28] Priya: what about model variants and quantization — if we fallback to a 13b quantized model how much latency improvement should we expect?
[04:35] Rita: typically 2-3x improvement in tokens/sec for int8/quantized paths on the same SKU, depending on kernel selection and sequence length. but need to validate with your prompt distribution.
[04:45] Marco: fallback decision path — is it automated by Redwood runtime or do we configure rules?
[04:50] Rita: both. we can define policy rules: threshold-based (queue depth or p95 crossing), plus model rollouts for canary. runtime can automatically route to pre-configured fallbacks or send 429s with retry headers. you can also opt for human-in-the-loop to flip modes during launches.
[05:06] Jules: audio was a bit garbled earlier, sorry — on telemetry, we need request-level cost attribution and per-route dashboards. is that in the console?
[05:13] Samir: yes, redwood console gives token-level cost breakdowns, per-route p95, and per-model usage. We'll include a short demo link in the follow-up.
[05:22] Priya: any concerns about data residency? some of our clients require EU-only processing.
[05:27] Avery: we can pin the POC to a specific region. Redwood supports region pinning and private deployment options if needed for later stages. we'll note region in the sizing worksheet.
[05:36] Marco: what about cold-starts for burst instances — how do you reduce latency from cold GPUs?
[05:40] Rita: two tactics: pre-warmed hot pool (kept with warmed KV cache and model loaded) and model variants with smaller memory footprint kept cold-provisioned for quick spin-up. also, prefix caching reduces warmup time for popular prompts.
[05:52] Priya: can we set a policy so that 25% of traffic is always routed to a quantized model for cost experiments?
[05:56] Rita: yes, can do traffic split / A/B and can tag to measure quality and latency differences.
[06:02] Jules: timeline — we'd like to start the POC next week, can that happen?
[06:06] Avery: yes. suggested timeline: Feb 12 - sizing worksheet and trace upload; Feb 16-17 - benchmark run; Feb 18-28 - short evaluation window + quality analysis; March 2 - POC review and decision. that fits within your month window?
[06:20] Jules: we can try, procurement may take a week but POC approvals are fast for proof-of-value.
[06:26] Marco: security doc handoff?
[06:28] Samir: we'll email SOC2, network diagram, and SSO/KMS integration notes immediately after the call.
[06:34] Priya: one more technical: do you support KV caching across shards or per-replica? how does your runtime keep coherence?
[06:40] Rita: currently per-serving shard with coordinated invalidation; for POC we'll show cache hit metrics and expected token savings. there are known edge cases with very long chats and we document invalidation heuristics.
[06:53] Jules: okay thanks. seems like we have alignment. a quick concern though — if burst is exhausted and we fallback to queueing, how will product show that to users without harming UX?
[07:02] Avery: product approach: typing indicator + partial streaming + notification that "processing is delayed" — that's less jarring than an error. we'll demo UX patterns in the follow-up deck.
[07:12] Marco: any regulatory logging implications with fallback model choices? must be auditable which model processed which request.
[07:18] Samir: yes audit logs include model id, model config, and request id. we'll surface that in the console and in the logs pack for compliance review.
[07:27] Priya: ok, last question — benchmarks: will you include p99? that's where we fail often.
[07:31] Rita: yes p99 will be captured; we typically run multiple replay windows to exercise tails and cold-start mix.
[07:38] Jules: excellent. let's recap next steps.
[07:41] Avery: recap: 1) I'll send the sizing worksheet and cost model by Feb 12. 2) Priya will upload anonymized 7-day traces by Feb 14. 3) Rita preps benchmark harness and GPU config by Feb 15. 4) Marco aligns on peering window by Feb 16. 5) Samir will schedule the 2-day benchmark (preferred Feb 16-17). 6) Redwood will send SOC2 and integration docs today.
[07:59] Jules: Yep, sounds good. thanks all.
[08:02] Priya: thanks.
[08:03] Marco: bye.
[08:04] Samir: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
